entry.title: IBM Bob On-Premises: Agentic AI Without Leaving Your Data Center

link.title: IBM Bob On-Premises: Agentic AI Without Leaving Your Data Center

entry.content:
Available from October 1st 2026, Bob On-Premises deploys the AI inference layer on your own Red Hat OpenShift cluster. The IDE experience is unchanged; only the backend moves inside your perimeter. Air-gap compatible.

This is the answer to the question I hear from every bank, insurer, and government customer: “Can Bob see our source code?” With On-Premises: no. Your RPG programs, COBOL, and business logic never leave the network.

The architecture made possible by the July 2026 decoupled design: IDE layer and inference layer are now fully separable. The IBM i AppMod lab below runs identically against a self-hosted backend.

→ Bob On-Premises documentation
entry.summary: IBM Bob On-Premises brings the full agentic AI coding assistant inside your own infrastructure — no data leaves your network. Critical for regulated industries, IBM i, and IBM Z shops.

entry.title: IBM Bob in EMEA: Leading the Agentic AI Wave in Enterprise

link.title: IBM Bob in EMEA: Leading the Agentic AI Wave in Enterprise

entry.content:
Bob is not a code-completion tool. It’s an agentic assistant — give it a goal, it plans and executes: reads your codebase, writes files, runs tests, iterates. After a year leading Bob adoption across EMEA, a few things are consistently true: the biggest value is collapsing time to understand legacy code from weeks to days; skills and MCP servers make it enterprise-grade; and the plan→review→execute loop is how you get adoption in regulated industries.

The flight400-demo is the scenario I run with customers: a fictional IBM i airline, Bob reading and explaining the RPG reservation logic, generating tests, then exposing an API — live, no pre-baked output.

IBM i is where Bob has the most impact. The codebase is old and dense, the developer pool is shrinking, and the platform is still better than anything that would replace it. Bob doesn’t replace IBM i. It makes it legible for the next generation.

→ IBM Bob documentation
entry.summary: What I've learned running IBM Bob with enterprise customers across EMEA — from first demos to production, and why IBM i is where Bob has the most impact.

entry.title: IBM Z Application Modernization with Bob

link.title: IBM Z Application Modernization with Bob

entry.content:
95% of ATM swaps, 80% of credit card transactions — IBM Z runs them. The problem isn’t that the code doesn’t work. It’s that the people who wrote it are retiring, and the codebases are essentially undocumented.

Bob on Z reads COBOL (including REDEFINES and nested PERFORM), parses JCL job streams, generates zUnit test stubs, and helps define z/OS Connect API wrappers to expose mainframe logic as REST endpoints. The lab in this repo walks through each step on a realistic workload.

The approach: strangler fig. Don’t replace. Wrap. Add tests. Expose APIs. Migrate individual services based on business priority.
entry.summary: Bob reads COBOL, explains JCL, generates zUnit tests, and scaffolds z/OS Connect REST APIs — making mainframe code legible and evolvable without a big-bang rewrite.

entry.title: IBM i for Beginners: The Most Underrated Platform in Enterprise IT

link.title: IBM i for Beginners: The Most Underrated Platform in Enterprise IT

entry.content:
IBM i (formerly AS/400) is an integrated OS where the database is built into the OS — not a separate product. Every object is typed. Db2 for i is the filesystem. Systems run for years without a reboot. It’s boring in the best possible way.

The ibmi-101 lab takes a developer from zero to their first RPG program, SQL query, and IFS file operation in a few hours. It runs on any trial IBM i system. It’s the starting point I use for every enablement session with developers who’ve never touched the platform.

Why learn it in 2026? IBM i skills are scarce, salaries are strong, and the modernization wave means there’s a generation of work ahead. If you know both RPG and the cloud-native world, you’re extremely valuable.
entry.summary: IBM i runs a surprising share of global commerce. Here's what it actually is, why it matters in 2026, and how to start learning it — with hands-on labs.

entry.title: IBM Redbook: Modernizing IBM i Applications with AI

link.title: IBM Redbook: Modernizing IBM i Applications with AI

entry.content:
IBM Redbooks are the authoritative technical deep-dives of the IBM ecosystem — peer-reviewed, field-tested, and built from real customer engagements. This one covers exactly what I do every day: taking decades of IBM i RPG and COBOL code, and making it legible, testable, and evolvable using AI.

I contributed to this Redbook alongside IBM colleagues and field engineers, drawing from the same customer projects and enablement sessions that underpin the posts on this blog. The content spans Bob-assisted code comprehension, RPGUnit test generation, DDS-to-DDL migration, REST API enablement with IWS, and Ansible Infrastructure as Code — a complete modernization playbook.

If you’re an IBM i shop wondering where to start with AI-assisted modernization, this is the reference document. Free, publicly available, and grounded in real IBM i workloads.

entry.title: IBM Bob Expands: Premium Packages, New Architecture, Enterprise Control

link.title: IBM Bob Expands: Premium Packages, New Architecture, Enterprise Control

entry.content:
The IBM i Developer and IBM Z modes are now premium packages — optional add-ons enterprise admins assign to specific users. A team of 200 doesn’t need IBM i premium; just the 30 who work on RPG do. This unlocked adoption at every organization that previously couldn’t justify company-wide licensing.

The new architecture decouples the IDE layer from the inference backend. This is what makes On-Premises possible: the IDE stays consistent, the AI runs wherever you need it — IBM Cloud, private watsonx.ai, or your own cluster.

Enterprise controls: shared Bobcoin pool, admin dashboard, team management, dedicated support. The full picture for a CIO: “Your RPG devs get IBM i premium. Your Java devs get AppMod. Your admin controls it from one dashboard.”

→ Full announcement
entry.summary: Premium packages for specialized domains (IBM i, IBM Z, Java), a new decoupled architecture, and centralized enterprise controls — the announcement that changed how I position Bob.

entry.title: IBM i Application Modernization with Bob

link.title: IBM i Application Modernization with Bob

entry.content:
The IBM i AppMod lab covers five stages: Bob reads and explains legacy RPG → generates RPGUnit tests → suggests DDS-to-DDL SQL migrations → produces an OpenAPI spec from service programs → scaffolds Ansible playbooks for system automation. Each step has a working exercise.

The key insight: time to understand is the real bottleneck. Once a team can read what the code does, every other modernization step accelerates dramatically. Bob collapses that from weeks to hours.

The companion flight400-demo runs this end-to-end on a fictional airline scenario — live, in Bob, with no pre-baked outputs. It’s the demo I use in every customer engagement.
entry.summary: The full IBM i modernization journey with Bob — code comprehension, RPGUnit test generation, DDS-to-DDL migration, REST API spec, and Ansible IaC. All from a single lab.

entry.title: IoT & Big Data: From Sensor to Dashboard, via IBM i

link.title: IoT & Big Data: From Sensor to Dashboard, via IBM i

entry.content:
The iot-bigdata-lab was built for IAE Montpellier MBA students: sensor → MQTT broker → Node-RED pipeline → dashboard, with IBM i Db2 providing the business context. The goal was to give non-developers a real mental model of what their engineers actually build.

The pattern matters beyond the classroom. Industrial IoT data (vibration, temperature, pressure) is only useful when joined with business context — maintenance history, asset SLAs, production orders — and that context almost always lives in IBM i. The vms-iot-dashboard project shows this in a real manufacturing scenario.

Node-RED remains my go-to prototyping tool. The node-red-contrib-db2-for-i node I published connects any Node-RED flow directly to IBM i Db2 — thousands of downloads, still used in production.
entry.summary: End-to-end IoT pipelines for engineering and business school students — MQTT, Node-RED, time-series storage, and real-time dashboards connected to IBM i business data.

entry.title: Cloud Design Patterns: Event-Driven, CDC, and Mesh Architectures

link.title: Cloud Design Patterns: Event-Driven, CDC, and Mesh Architectures

entry.content:
These patterns power the modernization projects I run with customers. The cdp-mesh-tutorial is the Polytech Montpellier course material — hands-on Kafka and CDC exercises on OpenShift, from zero to a running event-driven pipeline in a few hours.

The most impactful pattern for IBM i: Debezium CDC. Capture every Db2 for i journal record change and stream it to Kafka — zero polling, no ETL, real-time data propagation without touching the application. The debezium-ibmi-demo repo shows this end-to-end: IBM i journal → Debezium → Kafka → downstream consumers.

Data mesh is the next step: treating IBM i operational data as a domain-owned, catalogued data product, accessible to analytics and AI workloads via federated query — without copying it into a warehouse.
entry.summary: Real cloud design patterns from a Polytech Montpellier course — Kafka event streaming, Debezium CDC from IBM i, and data mesh concepts applied to enterprise modernization.
